evaluation_scope: These metrics measure citation and source-list alignment to dataset gold metadata (object id, act, section, where applicable pages). They do not evaluate full answer faithfulness, NLI-style grounding, or legal correctness of the prose beyond cited passages.

metric_notes.evaluation_scope: These metrics measure citation and source-list alignment to dataset gold metadata (object id, act, section, where applicable pages). They do not evaluate full answer faithfulness, NLI-style grounding, or legal correctness of the prose beyond cited passages.
metric_notes.citation_presence_rate: Share of non-blocked answers with model citation (indexes or used_source_ids) or bracket [n] in answer text.
metric_notes.model_citation_presence_rate: Non-empty used_source_indexes or used_source_ids in model JSON.
metric_notes.citation_validity_rate: Among rows with model citation: indices in [1, n_context] and every used_source_id appears on some retrieved chunk.
metric_notes.hallucinated_index_rate_micro: invalid index slots / count of used_source_indexes list entries (parse failures + OOB).
metric_notes.hallucinated_source_id_rate_micro: invalid used_source_ids / len(used_source_ids) summed over cited rows.
metric_notes.correct_citation_exact_match_rate: Among structurally valid cited rows with gold id: gold ∈ cited chunks via index or id.
metric_notes.correct_act_citation_rate: Among structurally valid cited rows with any cited chunk: act match (see code).
metric_notes.correct_page_citation_rate: Among structurally valid cited rows that have non-empty expected_page_numbers in the dataset: any cited chunk shares a page with expected.
metric_notes.gold_missing_from_citation_rate: Among structurally valid cited rows with gold id: gold object_id not in the cited union (indexes + valid used_source_ids).
metric_notes.soft_citation_support_rate: Same denominator as gold_missing_from_citation_rate: gold cited OR cited act+section matches expected (soft).
metric_notes.json_bracket_inconsistency_rate: Bracket [n] not subset of used_source_indexes or OOB.
